fields.meta_title: All About Me Questionnaire for Classes and Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an all about me questionnaire for students, new hires, campers, or mentees, with answers saved to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an All About Me Questionnaire That Gets Read After Day One
fields.hero_description: Build an all about me questionnaire whose answers reach the teacher, manager, or counselor who needs them, in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: An all about me questionnaire tells someone who a person is before they meet. Emergent builds the app that delivers the answers.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from who is answering

Describe who answers and who reads the answers, such as third graders and their teacher. Emergent builds the questions and the database behind them, and changes both on request.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen for children

Turn the questionnaire into a one-question-per-screen flow. A seven-year-old on a classroom tablet sees a single prompt, a few picture choices, and a large Next button.
fields.feature_3:
A roster that shows the whole group at once

Each response is saved as a row in a database you own. Read a class or a mentoring cohort as one roster, then open a single card to see every answer that person gave.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts sent to whoever reads the answers

Get a Slack message, an email, or an in-app alert each time someone submits. A team lead can read a new hire's answers the hour they come in, with no shared folder to check.
fields.feature_5:
Every family answers, with no cap

A school with 600 students or a camp running 12 summer sessions sends one questionnaire to all of them. Emergent sets no cap on responses, so late families still get in.
fields.feature_6:
Code that a district or HR team can host

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A school district's IT team can then host the questionnaire on its own servers and keep building on it.

fields.tab_content_1:
By week two, Ms. Delgado knows who is shy reading aloud

Ms. Delgado sends the questionnaire home in the first week at Maple Ridge Elementary, and each third grader answers with a parent. By Friday, 22 of the 24 have come back. Her roster shows that Owen learns best by building and is shy reading aloud. His first book report is a model he builds and explains to her alone.
fields.tab_content_2:
Priya is introduced to all 40 coworkers on day one

Corbel Analytics sends the questionnaire to each new hire once the offer is signed. Priya Raman, a data engineer, answers that she grew up in Tucson, bakes sourdough, and prefers written questions to calls. At 9:00 AM on her first day, the app posts her answers to #team in Slack, where 40 coworkers read them.
fields.tab_content_3:
Mira is Mimi to her counselor from the first morning

Pine Hollow Day Camp asks parents to answer the questionnaire for their child before the session starts. The counselor of the Otters, a group of 14 campers, opens one card per child on her phone at drop-off. Mira's card says she goes by Mimi, loves frogs, and brings a stuffed fox named Pepper that stays in her cubby.
fields.tab_content_4:
Andre's mentor is the one who also builds robots

Bright Path Mentors asks mentees and volunteer mentors the same questions about interests and goals. The app suggests a pair when two people share 2 or more interests. Andre, 15, shares robotics, hiking, and sci-fi with Lena, an engineer. The coordinator approves them, and their first meeting goes on the calendar.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an All About Me Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make an all about me questionnaire that puts each answer in front of the person who will act on it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep it to about ten questions
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the name they like first
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write a version for young children
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the reader, not the questions. A teacher planning seats needs different answers than a counselor at drop-off or a coordinator pairing mentors. Write down who opens the answers and what they will do with them in the first week.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep the questionnaire short enough to finish in one sitting. About ten questions leave room for a preferred name, a few favorites, how the person likes to learn or work, and one open question. Cut any question nobody will act on.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the preferred name at the top. It is the answer the reader uses most, and on a camp card or a class roster it becomes the label for the whole entry. Ask how to say it, too, if names in your group are often misread.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For children who cannot read the questions yet, write a parent version that asks on the child's behalf. For early readers, show one question per screen with picture choices. Keep the words short and put one choice on each screen.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Mark which answers the whole group can see and which only the reader sees. A new hire's hometown can go to the team channel. A student's worries belong with the teacher alone and stay off any shared board.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it before the first meeting
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the questionnaire before the start date, the first week of school, or the camp session. Answers that come in after the first meeting are too late to shape it. Remind anyone who has not answered after a few days.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the questionnaire, who answers it, and where the answers go. Emergent builds the questions, the database, and the view the reader opens, such as a roster, a Slack post, or a list of suggested pairs. Ask for any change in plain words.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an all about me questionnaire for my third grade class that asks each student how they learn best and what they love doing.

faq_plan.q: What is an all about me questionnaire?
How do I create an all about me questionnaire?

plan.angle: The search for all about me questionnaire returns printable worksheets for students and a few lists of icebreaker questions: a sheet that gets filled in once and then sits in a folder. None of them shows the answers being used after week one. This page shows the questionnaire as a small app for four people who need to know someone fast: a third grade teacher reading her class roster, an operations lead whose new hire is introduced in Slack on day one, a day camp counselor meeting campers by nickname, and a mentoring coordinator pairing mentees with mentors by shared interests. The FAQ covers which questions to ask, how many, young children, new hires, privacy and timing.
